title: Records for normalized supported localization at the four coefficient stages
statement: For categories $C,Z,U$ with inclusion functors into ambient categories, the first ambient category triangulated, define a supported localization to consist of $i^*,j^*,i_*,Rj_*,Ri^!$, the adjunctions $i^*\dashv i_*$, $j^*\dashv Rj_*$, $i_*\dashv Ri^!$, and a natural boundary completing the actual exceptional counit and open unit to a distinguished triangle. Require uniqueness of this boundary, $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Ri^!K[m],Rj_*j^*K)=0$, $Ri^!Rj_*G=0$, and invertibility of the exceptional unit. Define the Tor condition by preservation of the finite-Tor predicates and interval bounds $[a,b]$, $[a,b+N]$, $[a,b+N+1]$. For a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a separated finite-type map $t:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and complementary closed/open immersions $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, package these conditions in four coefficient-stage records. The finite record uses the actual intrinsic positive-quotient operations; the integral record uses completed operations, their limit realizations, finite records and normalized reductions; the rational record uses raw scalar localization and the specified pullbacks; the algebraically closed record uses common-stage inclusions and their unit/counit-normalized comparisons. All operations and coefficient categories are those in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], [def-weil-derived-direct-image], [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd], [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Define the integral exceptional tower by scalar restriction of finite exceptional values and conjugate the actual quotient transitions by the exceptional reduction comparisons; completeness transports its product and every projection to the displayed derived-limit triangle. Define the Weil record by functor and adjunction lifts to the fixed-pair categories with exactly the same underlying unit, counit and boundary.
